summary: Steel Blaw-Knox fire tower on Brush Mountain near Altoona, PA: built 1923 per FFLOS (late-1922 papers say recently erected). FFLOS says moved 1940 as Scalp Level; a 1945 item disputes this.

facts.design: Steel Blaw-Knox tower (FFLOS register); a steel cabin for the ranger stood at its base (1927 article)
facts.status_note: Register says it was moved in 1940 and renamed Scalp Level. A March 1945 item still places the tower on Brush Mountain, so the move date is disputed.

staffing.status: A ranger was on duty during the fire season (1927 article); a warden was to man the tower by October 1925; Jesse D. Brandt was assigned in April 1939; out of service in 1945 after vandal damage

facts.agency: State department of forests and waters, Pennsylvania (1927 article)

events.note: Register and a 1927 article give 1923; Altoona Mirror items from November and December 1922 describe it as nearly complete or recently erected
July 1924: $25 reward offered for information on people who broke into the cabin
November 1924 forest fire at the foot of the mountain burned more than 150 acres by midnight; flames were heading toward the tower
Forest fire warden to man the lookout by October 15, 1925
July 1927: man found guilty of defacing state property at the tower and fined $10; the charge alleged he cut his name and other marks on it
Jesse D. Brandt assigned to the tower, April 1939
Register says moved in 1940 and renamed Scalp Level; a March 1945 item still places the tower on Brush Mountain
March 1945: vandals badly damaged the tower; not in service that year; a patrolman was assigned instead

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and a March 1927 article date the tower to 1923; Altoona Mirror items from November and December 1922 describe it as nearly complete or recently erected. The record uses 1923 and the story mentions the 1922 reports.

sources.title: Brush Mountain
sources.publisher: Eastern US Lookouts (quoting Altoona newspapers, 1922 to 1945)

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: the register says moved in 1940 and renamed Scalp Level, but a March 1945 item says the tower was still on Brush Mountain and damaged. The Scalp Level site was not located in any source. The brief's coordinates (40.52173, -78.33219) are not from the register, which says no coordinates are available; verify before publishing. Newspaper text is as reproduced on the Eastern page; originals were not checked. Access and visit facts were not found, so they are omitted.
